answer: Stop sybils with an ivory seal, a timber bond, and a two-path echo check. Each identity locks one timber bond and receives one ivory seal that cannot be split, lent, or reused by another identity. Influence requires an echo: every attestation must be confirmed back along a different peer route with no shared funder, so a lone agent proves two independent paths. If N identities share a funder or an echo route, the ledger folds them into one seal, caps joint influence at one share, and slashes each bond by the folded size, so N clones stake N bonds for one share and lose N squared when caught.
